To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TEI-9646 and TEI-9667 are antagonistic to human vitamin D receptor (hVDR), whereas TEI-9645, TEI-9655 and TEI-9657 are agonistic to hVDR, depending on the amino acids at positions 305 and 397 of hVDR.
the agonistic or antagonistic activity of TE-9647 depends on the presence of His305, His397 and Cys403 or His305, Cys403 or/and Cys410 in the C-terminal of VDR.

the structural basis of the histamine-mediated vitamin D receptor (hVDR)-agonistic and antagonistic mechanism of (23S) 25-dehydro-19-nor-vitamin D3-26-23-lactone is that the compound forms an exo-methylene adduct with the hVDR and that this adduct formation depends on the presence of Cys410 or Cys403.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the structural basis of TEI-9687 antagonism and agonism in hVDR.
the molecular basis for the agonist and antagonist activity of TEI9647 and the role of the histidine residues in VDR.
the structural and functional basis of TEI- 9647 antagonistic action in human VDR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence or absence of His305, His397 and/or Cys403 or/and Cys410 in VDR is crucial to define the agonistic and antagonism of TEI- 9647.
the hydrogen bonds formed between TEI-9646 and His397, and His305, are the major determinants for agonistic and antagonisitc activities of TEI-9667, respectively.
the hydrogen bond between His305 and the 26-carbonyl group of TEI is the primary event for the antagonistic action of TEI- 9647.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TEI-9646 and TEI-9639 act as antagonists by a mechanism that involves covalent binding of these compounds to Cys403 or/and Cys410 in hVDR.
the agonistic/antagonistic activity of TEIs is dependent on the presence of His305, His397, Cys403 and/or Cys410 in hVDR.
the agonistic and antagonism of TEI- 9647 is caused mainly by the interactions with His305 and His397, respectively.

the hydrogen bonds formed between TEI-9646 and His305, and between TEI-9667 and His397, play crucial roles in determining the agonistic or antagonistic activity of TE1-9647.
a single amino acid substitution (F397H) is responsible for the agonistic activity in rVDR and the antagonistic activity in hVDR.
